title: For Trump, a Promised Economic Boom Collides With the Costs of War
partialText: President Trump said he had envisioned a growing economy and improving fortunes for American families in 2026. That appears at risk in his war with Iran.

title: Energy Secretary Says ‘No Guarantees’ Oil Prices Will Fall Soon
partialText: Energy Secretary Chris Wright said the Strait of Hormuz, a critical passageway for oil shipments, remained unsafe for tanker passage. Iran has been firing projectiles and laying mines.

title: FCC Chair Threatens to Revoke Broadcasters’ Licenses Over Iran War Coverage
partialText: The comment from Brendan Carr came on the heels of a social media message from President Trump criticizing the news media’s coverage of the war with Iran.

title: The Billionaire Backlash Against a Philanthropic Dream
partialText: The Giving Pledge, once trendy among the world’s richest, has come upon hard times.

title: It’s Good to Be a Billionaire, Even at Tax Time
partialText: Paying taxes would feel better if the truly rich were bearing a fair share, our columnist says.

title: Trump Administration Turns to Migrant Workers to Help Farm Labor Shortage
partialText: As the president’s immigration policies squeeze an already tight supply of farm labor, the Trump administration is making it cheaper to hire foreign farmworkers.

title: A Refugee Died After Border Patrol Left Him at a Cafe. Fear Followed.
partialText: Buffalo’s Arakan Rohingya community was rattled after a disabled man’s death. “Our worry comes from future incidents that may happen,” one resident said.

title: In Scolding the New U.S. Ambassador, South Africa Signals Defiance
partialText: The latest clash between the two countries illustrates the depths to which relations have sunk and the struggle to forge a new path forward.

title: In Texas, an Unyielding Gun Culture Jumps Off YouTube and Into Politics
partialText: Brandon Herrera, a Republican candidate for Congress, built a large online fan base as a “guntuber.”

title: The $500 Million Mystery Will, Signed by Ghosts
partialText: A seven-page document, mailed by an elusive figure, has set off a court battle over the estate of Tony Hsieh, the former chief executive of Zappos.

title: Why Minnesota Matters More Than Iran for America’s Future
partialText: Moms donating their breast milk to strangers, dads taking someone else’s kids to school: Minnesotans showed a basic human impulse to look out for their neighbors.

title: Timothée Chalamet Was Supposed to Be a New Kind of Leading Man
partialText: He’s no longer that heart-on-his-sleeve sensitive soft boy many people fell for.

title: And the Oscar Goes to …
partialText: A guide to the 2026 Academy Awards.

title: To Save His Life, Our Restaurant Critic Reset His Appetite
partialText: Pete Wells on the radical overhaul of his relationship with eating.

title: Commuters, Rejoice! The New Portal Bridge in New Jersey Is Ready for Riders.
partialText: The old Portal Bridge disrupted rail commutes in New Jersey for decades, frequently getting stuck when it swung to let boat traffic pass. Now a new bridge is open to the public.

title: Some Olympic Leaders Want to See Fixed Winter Games Host Cities
partialText: Fewer cities are bidding for Olympics, and those that are can’t always accommodate every event. The Milan-Cortina Games were the most sprawling Olympics in history.

title: It Was Going to Be Magic City Night at the Atlanta Hawks. Then the Outrage Poured In.
partialText: The famous strip club is a symbol of the authentic city to many people in Atlanta. But others wondered whether the N.B.A. should be promoting it.
